expected_level_description: You can: - describe different scripting tools and software that are available and currently in use
You can: - explain information security and the security controls available to protect solutions and services

You can: - build, configure, administer and support infrastructure solutions and services, for example, networking and physical infrastructure, commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) software, open source packages and solutions, or virtual and cloud computing
You can: - explain the most important principles of modern development standards and how they apply to your work - apply modern development standards principles under guidance
You can: - own an issue until a new owner has been found or the problem has been mitigated or resolved

You can: - investigate problems in systems, processes and services, with an understanding of the level of a problem, for example, strategic, tactical or operational - contribute to the implementation of remedies and preventative measures
You can: - take inputs and establish coherent frameworks that work

You can: - translate logical designs into physical designs - produce detailed designs - effectively document all work using required standards, methods and tools, including prototyping tools where appropriate - design systems characterised by managed levels of risk, manageable business and technical complexity, and meaningful impact - work with well understood technology and identify appropriate patterns
You can: - build and test simple interfaces between systems - work on more complex integration as part of a wider team
You can: - understand the core technical concepts related to the role, and apply them with guidance
You can: - correctly execute test scripts under supervision - understand the role of testing and how it works
You can: - troubleshoot and identify problems across different technology capabilities

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - explain common cyber threats such as phishing and ransomware - report a suspected security event
You can: - run vulnerability scans and report the results - track fixes with system owners
You can: - explain how health IT systems can harm patients, for example through wrong, missing, or delayed information - report a possible clinical safety issue through the right route
